pairs.english: to lock out and tag out

items.targetSentence: Usen guantes con el metal filoso.
items.englishTranslation: Wear gloves with the sharp metal.
items.explanation: The ustedes command 'Usen' comes first, and the adjective 'filoso' goes after the noun 'metal'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Dónde va el bajante?
items.englishTranslation: Where does the downspout go?
items.explanation: In questions with '¿Dónde?', the verb 'va' comes right after the question word, before the subject.

items.targetSentence: Falta una tapa en esta canaleta.
items.englishTranslation: An end cap is missing on this gutter.
items.explanation: 'Faltar' usually comes before what is missing: 'Falta una tapa', not 'Una tapa falta'.

items.targetSentence: Pongan sellador en el inglete.
items.englishTranslation: Put sealant on the miter.
items.explanation: 'Pongan' is the ustedes command of 'poner', and 'sellador' needs no article here because it means sealant in general.

items.targetSentence: Este gancho está flojo.
items.englishTranslation: This hanger is loose.
items.explanation: Use 'estar' (está) for a condition like loose, and 'este' agrees with the masculine noun 'gancho'.

items.targetSentence: Amarren la escalera con la cuerda.
items.englishTranslation: Tie off the ladder with the rope.
items.explanation: The command 'Amarren' comes first, then the thing you tie off, then 'con' and the tool.

items.targetSentence: No hay fuga en el codo.
items.englishTranslation: There is no leak at the elbow.
items.explanation: 'No' goes before 'hay', and after 'no hay' the noun 'fuga' usually takes no article.

items.targetSentence: ¿Tienes la cinta métrica?
items.englishTranslation: Do you have the tape measure?
items.explanation: 'Tienes' is the tú form for a coworker, and 'métrica' comes after 'cinta' and agrees with it.

items.targetSentence: Señora, hoy terminamos la limpieza.
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, today we finish the cleanup.
items.explanation: The present tense 'terminamos' can describe a plan for today, and 'hoy' goes before the verb.

items.targetSentence: La salida está tapada con hojas.
items.englishTranslation: The outlet is clogged with leaves.
items.explanation: 'Estar' plus the participle 'tapada' describes a state, and 'tapada' agrees with the feminine noun 'salida'.

items.targetSentence: Apaguen la máquina antes de limpiar.
items.englishTranslation: Turn off the machine before cleaning.
items.explanation: After 'antes de', Spanish uses the infinitive (limpiar), where English uses an -ing form.

items.targetSentence: ¿La escalera tiene base firme?
items.englishTranslation: Does the ladder have firm footing?
items.explanation: The adjective 'firme' comes after its noun 'base', and no article is needed before 'base' here.

items.targetSentence: Conecten el codo al bajante.
items.englishTranslation: Connect the elbow to the downspout.
items.explanation: 'A' + 'el' always contracts to 'al', so you say 'al bajante', not 'a el bajante'.

items.targetSentence: Hay madera podrida en la fascia.
items.englishTranslation: There is rotten wood on the fascia.
items.explanation: 'Hay' means 'there is', and the adjective 'podrida' comes after 'madera' and agrees with it in gender.

items.targetSentence: No suban con este viento.
items.englishTranslation: Don't go up in this wind.
items.explanation: In a negative ustedes command, 'No' goes right before the verb form 'suban'.

items.targetSentence: Pongan el bloque de salpicadura aquí.
items.englishTranslation: Put the splash block here.
items.explanation: 'Bloque de salpicadura' puts the main noun first and links the describing word with 'de'.

items.targetSentence: Necesitamos más bobinas de aluminio.
items.englishTranslation: We need more aluminum coils.
items.explanation: 'Más' goes before the noun, and the -amos ending already means 'we', so no 'nosotros' is needed.

items.targetSentence: Señor, ¿puede mover su carro?
items.englishTranslation: Sir, can you move your car?
items.explanation: 'Puede' (usted) comes before the infinitive 'mover', and the question mark opens at the start of the question, not the sentence.

items.targetSentence: Recojan los clavos con el imán.
items.englishTranslation: Pick up the nails with the magnet.
items.explanation: In the command 'Recojan', the g of 'recoger' changes to j before the a, and the verb comes first.

items.targetSentence: Revisen el rebosadero del parapeto.
items.englishTranslation: Check the overflow scupper on the parapet.
items.explanation: 'De' + 'el' contracts to 'del', and the owner noun, 'parapeto', comes after the thing that belongs to it.

items.targetSentence: Revisen la pendiente con el nivel.
items.englishTranslation: Check the slope with the level.
items.explanation: The ustedes command 'Revisen' comes first, then the object 'la pendiente', and the tool goes last after 'con el'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Quién trae las tijeras de hojalata?
items.englishTranslation: Who is bringing the tin snips?
items.explanation: '¿Quién' opens the question and takes a singular verb, 'trae'; 'de hojalata' comes after 'tijeras' to describe it.

items.targetSentence: Pónganse los lentes de seguridad.
items.englishTranslation: Put on your safety glasses.
items.explanation: With a command, the reflexive pronoun 'se' attaches to the end of the verb: 'Pónganse'.

items.targetSentence: Este tramo necesita dos bajantes.
items.englishTranslation: This run needs two downspouts.
items.explanation: 'Este' goes before the noun 'tramo', and the number 'dos' goes right before 'bajantes'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Le gusta este color, señora?
items.englishTranslation: Do you like this color, ma'am?
items.explanation: With 'gustar', the pronoun 'Le' (you, formal) comes before the verb, and the thing she likes, 'este color', comes after it.

items.targetSentence: Beto, sostén la escalera, por favor.
items.englishTranslation: Beto, hold the ladder, please.
items.explanation: Coworkers use tú, so the command is the short form 'sostén'; the name with a comma comes first.

items.targetSentence: Marquen la línea de tiza.
items.englishTranslation: Snap the chalk line.
items.explanation: 'Marcar' becomes 'Marquen' (c changes to qu) in the ustedes command; 'de tiza' goes after 'línea'.

items.targetSentence: La gárgola está bien sellada.
items.englishTranslation: The scupper is well sealed.
items.explanation: 'Estar' describes a condition; 'bien' goes before 'sellada', and 'sellada' is feminine because 'gárgola' is.

items.targetSentence: No corten sin las guardas.
items.englishTranslation: Don't cut without the guards.
items.explanation: For a negative command, put 'No' right before the command form 'corten'.

items.targetSentence: Cuidado con los cables eléctricos.
items.englishTranslation: Watch out for the power lines.
items.explanation: 'Cuidado con' means 'watch out for', and the adjective 'eléctricos' goes after the noun 'cables'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Están bien las hebillas del arnés?
items.englishTranslation: Are the harness buckles OK?
items.explanation: In a yes/no question the verb estar can come first, and de + el contracts to del.

items.targetSentence: Fijen los ganchos con tornillos.
items.englishTranslation: Fasten the hangers with screws.
items.explanation: The ustedes command fijen comes first, and the object los ganchos follows it.

items.targetSentence: El bajante no está derecho.
items.englishTranslation: The downspout isn't straight.
items.explanation: No goes right before the verb está, and the adjective derecho comes after it.

items.targetSentence: ¿Cuántos codos necesitamos aquí?
items.englishTranslation: How many elbows do we need here?
items.explanation: Cuántos and the noun stay together at the start, and the verb comes right after them.

items.targetSentence: Quiten la canaleta vieja primero.
items.englishTranslation: Remove the old gutter first.
items.explanation: The adjective vieja comes after the noun canaleta, and primero goes at the end.

items.targetSentence: Señor, ¿quiere ver el trabajo?
items.englishTranslation: Sir, do you want to see the work?
items.explanation: The question mark ¿ opens after the comma, and the infinitive ver follows quiere directly.

items.targetSentence: Prueben la salida con la manguera.
items.englishTranslation: Test the outlet with the hose.
items.explanation: Probar changes its stem to prueben in the command, and the tool comes after con.

items.targetSentence: La tapa necesita otro remache.
items.englishTranslation: The end cap needs another rivet.
items.explanation: Otro is used with no article, so you say otro remache, not un otro remache.

items.targetSentence: Pongan conos alrededor del elevador.
items.englishTranslation: Put cones around the lift.
items.explanation: Alrededor is followed by de, and de + el contracts to del.

items.targetSentence: No dejen chatarra en el pasto.
items.englishTranslation: Don't leave scrap metal on the grass.
items.explanation: For a negative ustedes command, put no before the verb, which has the same form as the positive one: no dejen.

items.targetSentence: Ayer instalamos los ganchos en la fascia nueva.
items.englishTranslation: Yesterday we installed the hangers on the new fascia.
items.explanation: Preterite 'instalamos' for a finished action; the adjective 'nueva' comes after 'fascia' and agrees with it in the feminine.

items.targetSentence: Vamos a poner el bloque de salpicadura aquí.
items.englishTranslation: We are going to put the splash block here.
items.explanation: Ir a + infinitive: 'vamos a poner' means 'we are going to put'; the place word 'aquí' goes at the end.

items.targetSentence: ¿Me puedes traer el sellador de la troca?
items.englishTranslation: Can you bring me the sealant from the truck?
items.explanation: The pronoun 'me' goes before the conjugated verb 'puedes', not after 'traer', in this order.

items.targetSentence: Apaguen la máquina antes de limpiar los rodillos.
items.englishTranslation: Turn off the machine before cleaning the rollers.
items.explanation: 'Apaguen' is the ustedes command; 'antes de' is followed by the infinitive 'limpiar'.

items.targetSentence: No suban al elevador sin el cordón de seguridad.
items.englishTranslation: Don't go up in the lift without the lanyard.
items.explanation: Negative ustedes command: 'No' plus 'suban'; 'a + el' contracts to 'al'.

items.targetSentence: Faltan dos codos para el bajante de atrás.
items.englishTranslation: Two elbows are missing for the back downspout.
items.explanation: 'Faltar' agrees with what is missing, so it is plural 'faltan' for 'dos codos', and it comes first.

items.targetSentence: Mañana llegamos temprano para quitar la canaleta vieja.
items.englishTranslation: Tomorrow we arrive early to remove the old gutter.
items.explanation: The time word 'mañana' opens the sentence; 'para' + infinitive gives the purpose, and 'vieja' follows 'canaleta'.

items.targetSentence: El inglete no encaja bien; lo cortamos otra vez.
items.englishTranslation: The miter doesn't fit well; we'll cut it again.
items.explanation: 'Lo' replaces 'el inglete' and goes before the verb 'cortamos'.

items.targetSentence: Pongan el rebosadero donde lo marca el plano.
items.englishTranslation: Put the overflow scupper where the plan marks it.
items.explanation: 'Lo' points back to 'el rebosadero' and goes before 'marca'; the subject 'el plano' comes after the verb.

items.targetSentence: Recojan la chatarra con el imán antes de salir.
items.englishTranslation: Pick up the scrap metal with the magnet before leaving.
items.explanation: 'Recojan' is the ustedes command of 'recoger' (g changes to j); 'antes de' takes the infinitive 'salir'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Ya revisaste la pendiente con el nivel?
items.englishTranslation: Did you already check the slope with the level?
items.explanation: "Ya" comes before the preterite verb, and "revisaste" is the tú preterite form for a coworker.

items.targetSentence: Ayer sellamos las tapas, pero una todavía gotea.
items.englishTranslation: Yesterday we sealed the end caps, but one is still dripping.
items.explanation: "Sellamos" after "Ayer" is the preterite, and "una" stands alone for "una tapa" because tapa is feminine.

items.targetSentence: Señora, vamos a cambiar el bajante de la esquina.
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, we are going to change the downspout at the corner.
items.explanation: Ir a + infinitive ("vamos a cambiar") talks about the plan; "bajante" takes the masculine article "el".

items.targetSentence: No corten la salida sin los lentes de seguridad.
items.englishTranslation: Don't cut the outlet without your safety glasses.
items.explanation: A negative ustedes command is "No" + "corten"; "sin" + article + noun gives "without the glasses".

items.targetSentence: Tenemos que mover la escalera lejos de los cables.
items.englishTranslation: We have to move the ladder away from the wires.
items.explanation: "Tener que" + infinitive means "have to"; "lejos" always needs "de" before the noun.

items.targetSentence: La gárgola está tapada; la limpio ahora mismo.
items.englishTranslation: The scupper is clogged; I'll clean it right now.
items.explanation: The object pronoun "la" (the scupper) goes before the conjugated verb "limpio", and "tapada" agrees with feminine gárgola.

items.targetSentence: ¿Cuántos ganchos faltan para el tramo del frente?
items.englishTranslation: How many hangers are missing for the front run?
items.explanation: "Faltan" is plural because the hangers are the subject; "de + el" contracts to "del".

items.targetSentence: Esta tarde vamos a soldar la canaleta de caja.
items.englishTranslation: This afternoon we are going to weld the box gutter.
items.explanation: The time phrase goes first, then ir a + infinitive; in "canaleta de caja" the type comes after the noun with "de".

items.targetSentence: Agarra el codo y sujétalo contra la pared.
items.englishTranslation: Grab the elbow and hold it against the wall.
items.explanation: In an affirmative tú command the pronoun attaches to the end of the verb: "sujétalo", with an accent added.

items.targetSentence: Inspector, ya pusimos el sellador en cada inglete.
items.englishTranslation: Inspector, we already put the sealant on every miter.
items.explanation: "Pusimos" is the irregular preterite of poner; "cada" goes before a singular noun with no article.

items.targetSentence: Antes de subir, revisen las hebillas del arnés.
items.englishTranslation: Before going up, check the buckles on the harness.
items.explanation: After 'antes de' Spanish uses the infinitive (subir), and 'de + el' contracts to 'del'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Dónde vamos a poner la salida de esta canaleta?
items.englishTranslation: Where are we going to put the outlet for this gutter?
items.explanation: The future 'ir a + infinitive' stays together: vamos a poner, with the question word first.

items.targetSentence: Señor Ruiz, mañana le instalamos los protectores de canaleta.
items.englishTranslation: Mr. Ruiz, tomorrow we'll install the gutter guards for you.
items.explanation: The indirect object pronoun 'le' (for you, usted) goes right before the conjugated verb.

items.targetSentence: No dejen las tijeras de hojalata en el techo.
items.englishTranslation: Don't leave the tin snips on the roof.
items.explanation: A negative ustedes command puts 'no' before the verb: no dejen.

items.targetSentence: Tienes que secar la junta antes de poner sellador.
items.englishTranslation: You have to dry the joint before putting on sealant.
items.explanation: 'Tener que' is followed by an infinitive: tienes que secar.

items.targetSentence: Beto, la bobina café se terminó; avísale al chofer.
items.englishTranslation: Beto, the brown coil ran out; let the driver know.
items.explanation: The color goes after the noun (bobina café), and the pronoun attaches to the tú command: avísale.

items.targetSentence: Los ganchos ocultos van dentro de la canaleta.
items.englishTranslation: The hidden hangers go inside the gutter.
items.explanation: The adjective comes after the noun and matches it in number and gender: ganchos ocultos.

items.targetSentence: Inspector, ¿quiere ver la caja colectora del almacén?
items.englishTranslation: Inspector, do you want to see the conductor head on the warehouse?
items.explanation: The usted form 'quiere' is used for the inspector, and the question mark opens after the comma.

items.targetSentence: Ana, ¿lo apuntaste en la lista de pendientes?
items.englishTranslation: Ana, did you write it down on the punch list?
items.explanation: The object pronoun 'lo' comes before the preterite verb apuntaste.

items.targetSentence: Pongan los conos alrededor del elevador antes de subir.
items.englishTranslation: Put the cones around the lift before going up.
items.explanation: 'Alrededor de' is followed by the noun, and 'de + el' becomes 'del'.

items.targetSentence: Luis, amarra la escalera antes de subir al alero.
items.englishTranslation: Luis, tie off the ladder before going up to the eave.
items.explanation: After 'antes de' Spanish uses the infinitive (subir), and 'a + el' contracts to 'al'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Por qué no baja el agua por la salida?
items.englishTranslation: Why isn't the water going down through the outlet?
items.explanation: In questions the verb (baja) comes before the subject (el agua), and 'no' goes right before the verb.

items.targetSentence: Ayer reemplazamos los codos abollados del lado derecho.
items.englishTranslation: Yesterday we replaced the dented elbows on the right side.
items.explanation: The adjective 'abollados' follows the noun and agrees with it in the masculine plural; 'reemplazamos' is preterite here.

items.targetSentence: Voy a medir el tramo del lado izquierdo.
items.englishTranslation: I'm going to measure the run on the left side.
items.explanation: 'Ir a + infinitive' expresses a near future: voy a medir.

items.targetSentence: Señora, la extensión de bajante protege sus cimientos.
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, the downspout extension protects your foundation.
items.explanation: 'Extensión de bajante' puts the main noun first; 'sus' is the polite possessive for usted.

items.targetSentence: Necesitamos más tapas blancas; pídelas al proveedor, por favor.
items.englishTranslation: We need more white end caps; order them from the supplier, please.
items.explanation: The pronoun 'las' attaches to the end of an affirmative command (pídelas), and the accent is added to keep the stress.

items.targetSentence: No doblen la lámina sin guantes; corta mucho.
items.englishTranslation: Don't bend the sheet metal without gloves; it cuts a lot.
items.explanation: A negative ustedes command uses the subjunctive form: no doblen.

items.targetSentence: El viento está fuerte; bajen de la escalera ahora.
items.englishTranslation: The wind is strong; get down from the ladder now.
items.explanation: 'Estar' describes the current condition of the wind; 'bajar de' means to get down from.

items.targetSentence: Marquen el punto alto con el marcador rojo.
items.englishTranslation: Mark the high point with the red marker.
items.explanation: Adjectives follow their nouns (punto alto, marcador rojo); 'marcar' changes c to qu in 'marquen'.

items.targetSentence: ¿Le confirmaste el color de la canaleta al cliente?
items.englishTranslation: Did you confirm the gutter color with the customer?
items.explanation: The indirect object pronoun 'le' goes before the verb and repeats 'al cliente', which is normal in Spanish.

items.targetSentence: Antes de que llueva, terminen de sellar las uniones de la canaleta.
items.englishTranslation: Before it rains, finish sealing the gutter joints.
items.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive (llueva), and terminar de goes before the infinitive sellar.

items.targetSentence: Es importante que usen guantes cuando corten la bobina de aluminio.
items.englishTranslation: It is important that you wear gloves when you cut the aluminum coil.
items.explanation: Es importante que triggers the subjunctive (usen), and cuando about a future action also takes it (corten).

items.targetSentence: ¿Podría mover su carro de la entrada para que pase la troca?
items.englishTranslation: Could you move your car out of the driveway so the truck can get through?
items.explanation: The conditional podría makes a polite request, and para que needs the subjunctive pase, with the subject after the verb.

items.targetSentence: Si ven cables eléctricos cerca, no levanten la canaleta hasta que yo avise.
items.englishTranslation: If you see power lines nearby, don't lift the gutter until I give the word.
items.explanation: Si takes the present indicative (ven), but hasta que about a future moment takes the subjunctive (avise).

items.targetSentence: Cuando terminen de soldar la canaleta de caja, revisen cada junta.
items.englishTranslation: When you finish welding the box gutter, check every joint.
items.explanation: Cuando about a future action uses the subjunctive terminen, and the command revisen comes after the comma.

items.targetSentence: No instalen el rebosadero hasta que el contratista general confirme la altura.
items.englishTranslation: Don't install the overflow scupper until the general contractor confirms the height.
items.explanation: No goes before the command instalen, and hasta que takes the subjunctive confirme for something that hasn't happened yet.

items.targetSentence: Necesito que me sostengas el codo mientras pongo los remaches.
items.englishTranslation: I need you to hold the elbow for me while I put in the rivets.
items.explanation: Necesito que triggers the subjunctive sostengas, and the pronoun me goes before the conjugated verb.

items.targetSentence: Pongan el bloque de salpicadura para que no se forme un charco.
items.englishTranslation: Put the splash block in place so that a puddle doesn't form.
items.explanation: Para que needs the subjunctive forme, and no and se both go before the verb, in that order.

items.targetSentence: Si usted prefiere el color café, tendríamos que pedir otra bobina al proveedor.
items.englishTranslation: If you prefer the brown color, we would have to order another coil from the supplier.
items.explanation: The conditional tendríamos softens the answer to the customer, and the color word café goes after the noun color.

items.targetSentence: ¿Revisaron los controles del elevador antes de que suba el operador?
items.englishTranslation: Did you check the lift controls before the operator goes up?
items.explanation: Antes de que takes the subjunctive suba, and the subject el operador usually comes after the verb.

items.targetSentence: Quiero que marquen la línea de tiza antes de poner los ganchos.
items.englishTranslation: I want you to snap the chalk line before putting up the hangers.
items.explanation: Querer que + a different subject needs the subjunctive: marquen, not marcan.

items.targetSentence: Señora, ¿podría dejar la puerta cerrada mientras quitamos la canaleta vieja?
items.englishTranslation: Ma'am, could you keep the door closed while we remove the old gutter?
items.explanation: The conditional podría makes a polite request; the adjective cerrada follows the noun puerta.

items.targetSentence: Si falta una tapa, avísenme antes de que suban la canaleta.
items.englishTranslation: If an end cap is missing, let me know before you lift the gutter up.
items.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive (suban), and the pronoun me attaches to the command avísenme.

items.targetSentence: No conectes el bajante hasta que el sellador de la salida esté seco.
items.englishTranslation: Don't connect the downspout until the sealant on the outlet is dry.
items.explanation: A negative tú command uses the subjunctive (no conectes), and hasta que about the future also takes the subjunctive (esté).

items.targetSentence: Conviene que alineen cada gancho con la marca antes de atornillarlo.
items.englishTranslation: You should line up each hanger with the mark before screwing it in.
items.explanation: Conviene que triggers the subjunctive (alineen); the pronoun lo attaches to the infinitive atornillarlo.

items.targetSentence: ¿Le molestaría si movemos sus macetas para poner la escalera?
items.englishTranslation: Would you mind if we move your flowerpots to set up the ladder?
items.explanation: The pronoun le goes before the conditional molestaría, making a polite request to one customer.

items.targetSentence: Mantengan tres puntos de apoyo cuando suban por la escalera.
items.englishTranslation: Keep three points of contact when you climb the ladder.
items.explanation: Cuando about a future or habitual action in a command takes the subjunctive: suban, not suben.

items.targetSentence: Limpien la gárgola para que el agua salga del techo plano.
items.englishTranslation: Clean the scupper so that the water drains off the flat roof.
items.explanation: Para que always takes the subjunctive (salga); de + el contracts to del.

items.targetSentence: ¿Qué pendiente pide el plano para que el agua corra a la salida?
items.englishTranslation: What slope does the plan call for so that the water runs to the outlet?
items.explanation: In the question, the verb pide comes before its subject el plano; para que needs the subjunctive corra.

items.targetSentence: Cuando llegue el inspector, le mostramos los ingletes y las tapas selladas.
items.englishTranslation: When the inspector arrives, we'll show him the miters and the sealed end caps.
items.explanation: Cuando about a future event takes the subjunctive (llegue), and le goes before the conjugated verb mostramos.

items.targetSentence: Amarren la escalera al alero antes de que alguien empiece a subir.
items.englishTranslation: Tie the ladder off to the eave before anyone starts to climb.
items.explanation: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, so it is 'empiece', not 'empieza'.

items.targetSentence: Si la fascia está podrida, tomen una foto antes de poner ganchos.
items.englishTranslation: If the fascia is rotten, take a photo before putting up hangers.
items.explanation: After si, use the present indicative ('está'); 'antes de' is followed by an infinitive when there is no new subject.

items.targetSentence: ¿Le gustaría que instaláramos protectores de canaleta en la parte de atrás?
items.englishTranslation: Would you like us to install gutter guards on the back?
items.explanation: A conditional like 'gustaría' followed by que takes the past subjunctive: 'instaláramos'.

items.targetSentence: Revisa que el inglete encaje bien antes de poner el sellador.
items.englishTranslation: Check that the miter fits well before putting on the sealant.
items.explanation: 'Revisa que' gives an instruction about a result, so the verb after it is subjunctive: 'encaje'.

items.targetSentence: El contratista quiere que la membrana quede debajo de la canaleta de caja.
items.englishTranslation: The contractor wants the membrane to sit under the box gutter.
items.explanation: Querer que with a new subject needs the subjunctive: 'quede'. 'Canaleta de caja' keeps the noun first.

items.targetSentence: Bajen la plataforma ahora porque el viento está muy fuerte.
items.englishTranslation: Lower the platform now because the wind is very strong.
items.explanation: Porque gives a fact, so it takes the indicative ('está'); 'Bajen' is the ustedes command.

items.targetSentence: ¿Cuántos codos vamos a necesitar si el bajante baja por esta esquina?
items.englishTranslation: How many elbows are we going to need if the downspout runs down this corner?
items.explanation: 'Cuántos' agrees with masculine plural 'codos'; the si clause uses the present indicative.

items.targetSentence: Ponle sellador a cada tapa para que no gotee en la punta.

items.phraseTranslation: Before cleaning the rollers, it is necessary that Pedro [verb] the machine.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'es necesario que' (present) triggers the subjunctive, and the subject 'Pedro' is singular.

items.phrase: Ayer el supervisor nos pidió que ___ el frente dos veces antes de cortar la pieza, y así lo hicimos.
items.phraseTranslation: Yesterday the supervisor asked us to [verb] the front twice before cutting the piece, and we did.
items.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive: the past request 'pidió que' requires the past subjunctive, and 'nos' makes the subject nosotros.

items.phrase: Es imposible que la canaleta ___ la prueba con la manguera si el inglete no tiene sellador.
items.phraseTranslation: It is impossible for the gutter to [verb] the hose test if the miter has no sealant.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'es imposible que' always triggers the subjunctive, and 'la canaleta' is singular.

items.phrase: Si ustedes instalaran el codo al revés, el agua ___ por la junta.
items.phraseTranslation: If you installed the elbow backwards, the water would [verb] through the joint.
items.explanation: Conditional: the hypothetical 'si' clause with 'instalaran' takes the conditional result, and 'el agua' is singular.

items.phrase: Mientras Beto llamaba al 911, Pedro ___ la ambulancia en la calle.
items.phraseTranslation: While Beto was calling 911, Pedro [verb] for the ambulance in the street.
items.explanation: Imperfect indicative: 'mientras' with 'llamaba' describes two ongoing past actions, and 'Pedro' is singular.

items.phrase: No suelten el bajante hasta que las abrazaderas lo ___ bien a la pared.
items.phraseTranslation: Don't let go of the downspout until the straps [verb] it firmly to the wall.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'hasta que' about a future event in a present command triggers the subjunctive, and 'las abrazaderas' is plural.

items.phrase: Si tuviéramos la bobina blanca en el tráiler, nosotros ___ la bobina café ahora mismo.
items.phraseTranslation: If we had the white coil in the trailer, we [verb] the brown coil right now.
items.explanation: Conditional: 'si' + imperfect subjunctive (tuviéramos) calls for the conditional in the result, and nosotros is the subject.

items.phrase: Es importante que la salida ___ libre de hojas antes de probar la canaleta.
items.phraseTranslation: It is important that the outlet [verb] free of leaves before testing the gutter.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'Es importante que' in the present triggers it, and 'la salida' is singular.

items.phrase: Ayer el supervisor no dejó que nadie ___ al techo hasta que pasó la tormenta.
items.phraseTranslation: Yesterday the supervisor didn't let anyone [verb] onto the roof until the storm passed.
items.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive: past 'no dejó que' triggers it, and 'nadie' takes a singular verb.

items.phrase: Antes de que tú te ___ el arnés, revisa bien las hebillas.
items.phraseTranslation: Before you [verb] the harness, check the buckles carefully.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'antes de que' always takes subjunctive, and the subject is tú, in the present with the command 'revisa'.

items.phrase: Yo que ustedes, ___ la escalera lejos de los cables eléctricos antes de subir.
items.phraseTranslation: If I were you, I [verb] the ladder away from the power lines before climbing.
items.explanation: Conditional: 'Yo que ustedes' gives advice in the conditional, and the speaker (yo) is the subject.

items.phrase: Necesito que Beto y Ana ___ la canaleta en la línea de tiza mientras yo atornillo el gancho.
items.phraseTranslation: I need Beto and Ana to [verb] the gutter on the chalk line while I screw in the hanger.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'Necesito que' in the present triggers it, and 'Beto y Ana' is a plural subject.

items.phrase: Si el código local ___ otra cosa, cambiaríamos la pendiente de la canaleta.
items.phraseTranslation: If the local code [verb] something else, we would change the slope of the gutter.
items.explanation: Imperfect subjunctive: a 'si' clause paired with the conditional 'cambiaríamos' needs it, and 'el código' is singular.

items.phrase: Cuando ustedes ___ los codos con remaches, llámenme para revisar el bajante.
items.phraseTranslation: When you [verb] the elbows with rivets, call me to check the downspout.
items.explanation: Present subjunctive: 'cuando' about a future action takes subjunctive, and the subject is ustedes.
